findings.title: Duplicate downsize definition deletes 4-arg API
findings.body: The file now defines self.downsize twice: once as downsize(from,to,max_width,max_height,opts) and immediately again as downsize(from,to,dimensions,opts). Ruby has no overloading, so the second definition overwrites the first and the first becomes dead code. Any existing caller using the width/height pair form will get ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments) after this merge. Only the new percent-string form works.

findings.title: In-place downsize overwrites source file
findings.body: create_upload calls OptimizedImage.downsize with tempfile.path as both source and destination. ImageMagick convert reading and writing the same path is unsafe, and if conversion fails the original upload bytes are already truncated or destroyed. Upload.create_for then stores the corrupt/truncated file, causing permanent data loss for that upload. A separate temp output file that is only moved into place on success is required.

findings.title: Loop ignores downsize failure and checks stale size
findings.body: The while loop checks tempfile.size on the open File handle while the external convert command rewrites the file via its path, so the observed size can stay stale if the converter replaces the inode, and the boolean return value of downsize is never checked. The loop therefore can run all 5 iterations even when the first pass already brought the file under the limit or when conversion keeps failing, shrinking images to about 0.8^5 of dimensions unnecessarily, wasting 5 ImageMagick runs, and passing a stale size to Upload.create_for.

findings.title: Animated GIFs stripped and SVGs rasterized by downsize
findings.body: The downsize gate fires for any filename where FileHelper.is_image? is true, including .gif and .svg, with no special case. Animation selection in OptimizedImage.optimize checks the source path for /.GIF$/i, but here the source is tempfile.path which is a generated RackMultipart or download name without the original extension, so it never matches. The fallback ImageMagick command uses from[0] which keeps only the first frame, silently destroying animation even when allow_animated_thumbnails is true. SVGs which are copied verbatim elsewhere are sent through convert and rasterized. The animated branch also delegates to gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH, not the passed 80% string.

findings.title: Hardcoded 10MB client limit breaks per-type site settings
findings.body: validateUploadedFile replaced Discourse.SiteSettings['max_'+type+'_size_kb'] with a fixed 10*1024 for both images and attachments, and the 413 handler similarly hardcodes max_image_size_kb. Sites with max_attachment_size_kb different from 10MB now validate attachments incorrectly, either allowing files the server will reject or rejecting files the server would allow, and sites with max_image_size_kb larger than 10MB incorrectly reject images on the client.

findings.title: URL download cap ignores larger configured image limit
findings.body: FileHelper.download for API URL uploads was changed from SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes to a fixed 10.megabytes. On sites where the administrator configured max_image_size_kb larger than 10MB, remote URL uploads between 10MB and the configured limit will now fail or be truncated even though they are allowed. The limit should be the maximum of the configured setting and the auto-downsize allowance.
